summary: The text argues for continued funding of E-Rate to ensure school districts and public libraries can maintain current levels of access and improve student learning, emphasizing the long-term economic and defense impacts of eliminating E-Rate funding.

claims.argument: Continued funding is vital for school districts and public libraries to maintain current levels of access and improve student learning
claims.evidence_quote: In the overall context of the federal budget, E-Rate represents an insignificant expenditure, but in the reality of the work of school districts and public libraries, the loss of E-Rate would absolutely cripple our efforts to stay-up-to-date with technology, with Internet access, and with improving and deepening student learning.
